title: Replicated traffic safety gate and cost governor for model mirroring
creator: Asha Kapoor
body:
Summary:
We need a robust safety gate for replicated (shadow/duplicated) inference traffic that enforces per-tenant cost budgets, rate-limits sampling, and isolates side-effects from production paths. This ticket implements the control-plane and lightweight data-plane hooks for a Replication Safety Gate and an associated Cost Governor to prevent runaway spend and noisy neighbors during mirroring experiments and canary workflows.

Motivation:
- Shadowing is essential for pre-production validation, but duplicate requests can sharply increase GPU costs and cross-tenant interference.
- Existing duplication logic lacks per-tenant budgeting and a global backpressure signal. We need explicit quota enforcement, kill-switches, and observable accounting for mirrored paths.

Goals (non-exhaustive):
1) Provide per-tenant replication budget (tokens/credits) that is decremented on mirrored requests and refuses mirrors when budget exhausted.
2) Support declarative sampling strategies: fixed-rate, stratified-by-route, and dynamic-budget-paced sampling.
3) Ensure safe request isolation: replicated requests must not trigger side-effects (DB writes, external API calls) in the target environment; enforce via headers and runtime checks.
4) Implement a global cost-governor that can throttle replication cluster-wide under abnormal spend.
5) Produce end-to-end telemetry: tokens consumed, sampling rate, cost-per-tenant, queueing latency, and number of dropped mirrors.

Proposed design:
- Control plane: New ReplicationPolicy resource (API + DB table) bound to customer/route that specifies budget_quota (tokens/month), sampling_strategy (fixed|stratified|budgeted), max_in_flight_mirrors, and fallback policy (drop|queue|route-to-cheaper-model).
- Data plane enforcement: At gateway, a ReplicationGate short-circuits duplication if: tenant budget exhausted, global governor in reduced mode, or tenant flagged for quarantine. The gate consults a local in-memory token bucket synced from the control plane with eventual consistency (refresh interval 10s).
- Sampling implementation: For budgeted sampling, mirror attempts consume a token; sampling probability is min(request_weight / unit_cost, remaining_budget / lookahead_window). To limit cost spikes, we cap per-route sampled tokens per-second to configurable limits.
- Tenant isolation: Add a required header X-Replication-Safe: true and X-Replication-Mode: readonly to be propagated to mirrored services. Runtime asserts in the serving runtime will EITHER drop outbound side-effecting calls OR route them to a sandbox endpoint. Non-compliant models will be quarantined.
- Global cost governor: A controller monitors cluster spending (estimated GPU-seconds * model-profile-cost) and can push the system into states: NORMAL, CONSERVATIVE, EMERGENCY. In CONSERVATIVE mirroring is reduced by a factor; in EMERGENCY, all non-critical mirroring is disabled.

Telemetry and SLOs:
- Metrics required: replication_tokens_consumed{tenant,route}, mirrored_requests_dropped{reason}, mirrored_cost_estimate{tenant}, replication_queue_depth, replication_latency_p95.
- Alerts: (1) mirrored_cost_estimate increase > 30% vs baseline for 5m -> Pager, (2) tokens_depletion_rate > 80% for a tenant -> PM/owner notify, (3) global governor emergency -> Pager.

Acceptance criteria:
- Gateway enforces per-tenant budget: when budget hits zero, duplicates are refused and a metric is emitted.
- Sampling strategies selectable per-route via ReplicationPolicy and exercised in e2e test harness.
- Replicated requests carry X-Replication-* headers and are blocked from making write-side effects in the sandboxed target (cannot call external webhook in integration tests).
- Global cost governor can transition to CONSERVATIVE and EMERGENCY states via a manual toggle and automatically by cost thresholds.
- Dashboards show per-tenant cost and tokens; alerts fire for the three conditions above.

Implementation plan (phases):
A) Small experiment: add budget check in gateway, implement fixed-rate sampling and a debug endpoint to drain tokens. (2 weeks)
B) Policy API and DB schema + sync agent for in-memory token buckets. (1 week)
C) Dynamic/budgeted sampling and quota accounting + unit tests. (2 weeks)
D) Tenant isolation enforcement and runtime assertion hooks. (1 week)
E) Global governor, dashboards, and alerting. (2 weeks)
F) Canary rollout: enable for internal tenants only -> 2-week burn -> expand.

Testing and QA:
- Unit tests for token accounting and sampling math.
- Integration tests that simulate high-volume traffic and verify that mirrored cost stays within quota and governor transitions fire.
- Chaos test: force token-store lag to verify graceful behavior (fail-open vs fail-closed toggles).

Rollout and rollback strategy:
- Feature gate behind a runtime flag. Start with internal tenants (redwood-internal) at 100% mirroring allowed but counted. Next enable enforcement for 10% of eligible tenants. Monitor cost/drops for 72 hours.
- Auto-rollback: if mirrored_cost_estimate for new policy exceeds baseline by >50% for 15m or number of dropped mirrors > predefined threshold that impacts SLAs, automatically cut mirroring to 0% and create incident.

Risks and trade-offs:
- Conservative token sync window (10s) trades immediate accuracy for throughput; we accept short windows of over-mirroring for lower API latency.
- Budget-driven sampling requires careful cost-estimation per-request; inaccurate models can lead to premature depletion. We'll start with coarse unit_costs and iterate.

Notes and links:
- This ticket intentionally separates enforcement (gateway) from orchestration (control plane) to keep the hot path minimal.
- Look at ENG-7642 and ENG-51234 for historical shadowing components we can reuse.

2025-11-13 - Security review (prelim): Require X-Replication-Safe header enforcement and audit log entries for mirrored requests that attempted external calls. Security to re-review after sandbox hooks implemented.
